newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cossack production back to normal - Woodside.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cossack production back to normal - Woodside.

text.p: Crude production from the Cossack Pioneer floating oil rig had recommenced and was back at average daily levels of 95,000 to 100,000 barrels, the operator, Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Monday.
When asked if the rig was back to normal production levels, a Woodside spokesman said: "Oh yes."
The rig, which disconnected a week ago from its mooring on the North West Shelf to flee the path of a cyclone, restarted at 6.30 p.m. local time (1030 GMT) on Friday, the spokesman said.
One cargo of just over 600,000 barrels already had been offloaded from the rig, he said, declining to disclose its destination.
The cyclone ran out of steam by mid last week after touching land near Port Hedland, Western Australia.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf, where the Cossack Pioneer is situated, are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
